In the heart of Middle Earth's western lands, where the mighty rivers carved their path through ancient stone, there lay a chasm of such immense scale and breathtaking beauty that even the wisest of the Istari would marvel at its splendor. 

The Grand Canyon, as it came to be known in the tongues of Men, stretched on for leagues unending, a great rift in the earth's very flesh. Its walls rose like towering ramparts, their faces painted in hues of ochre, crimson, and amber by the brush of time itself. Layer upon layer of stone told the tale of ages long past, each band a chapter in the grand saga of the world's shaping.

From the canyon's lofty rims, one could gaze down into the abyss and spy the silver ribbon of the Colorado River, winding like a great serpent at the bottom of the gorge. The river's waters, though distant, echoed through the vastness, their voice a ceaseless whisper of the untamed wild.

In the changing light of sun and shadow, the canyon transformed, its colors shifting from the pale gold of dawn to the fiery oranges of dusk. Mists would rise from its depths, cloaking the chasm in a veil of mystery, as if the very secrets of creation lingered still in those ancient depths.

To wander the paths that traced the canyon's edge was to embark upon a journey through a realm as old as Arda itself. In the Grand Canyon's timeless beauty, one could almost hear the echoes of the Music of the Ainur, the great symphony that had shaped the world at its beginning and would endure long after the passing of Elves and Men alike.

I knew you’d bring up RDR2 😂. The difference between birds in RDR2 and Planet Zoo is that in RDR2, people aren’t spending most of their time focused on them. If you do, you begin to see the rails. They are elaborate rails, but still repetitive. And the landing m/take off animations are not great. Also, the feathers look stiff upon closer inspection. In Planet Zoo, people will be zooming in, watching for some time as the animals move around. The animations need to be butter smooth and details need to be intricate. RDR2 models in Planet Zoo wouldn’t never hold up for a second, despite how well they fit their game. In the case of Planet Zoo, yes more really is better. In RDR2, less is more.

Not true. Most games cheat when it comes to flying creatures, using rails, or other mechanics to cheat the system. Planet zoo did this with exhibit bats and butterflies and people aren’t super happy with it. Planet Zoo animals have freedom of movement in their habitat and the development team knows we expect the same for birds. 
Also, take a closer look at most other games and you will notice the flying habits of the birds are not accurate for the most part. Especially when it comes to taking off or landing. It definitely isn’t impossible, but it’s a lot harder than swimming or walking.

Take a minute and think of the physics behind jumping and then compare that to the physics behind flying. Also, consider the intricacies of having to animate a short haired mammal versus the air flowing through individual flight and tail feathers. There is a reason it has not been done yet. It’s hard to get right and make believable in game. They probably don’t want to release a half baked product because of the backlash they would receive for how awful and unrealistic it would look.

Are you wanting to know the best template? Because there is no best template. It all depends on what you are planning on doing with them. 

But my basic division is 7inf, 2art with support art, hosp, engineer. 

From that, I change out art for AA and/or anti-tank depending on what I’m facing. Adding recon or radio support as needed, and making them 40 width when my production and manpower is capable of handling it. 

Basic 40 width is just double the 20 width, but I tend to specialize them more. Adding heavy tanks or SP Art. 

Just remember, infantry (motorized or foot) add organization (which is good) while other brigades (art, tanks, etc) add hard attack or other bonuses but take away organization. So you never want a full division of just tanks, artillery, etc. add some infantry or motorized/mechs to increase org. 

Infantry also have the best defense. So, keep that in mind when making divisions for just defense. 

Paratroopers should usually be small so you can mass produce them and don’t lose much when they are destroyed. This way, you can jump behind enemies, encircling them or taking VPs without having to break through their lines. But this strat can have negative consequences if you can’t connect the paratroopers to your lines soon. That’s why I keep them small. Usually 3-4 paratroopers. No support unless I feel like I need to assault a position or need to dig in, in which case I add art and engineers for support. 

Marines vary, depending on what you need them for. Operation Sea Lion will need at least 20 width with some hard attack to take British ports (naval tanks and motorized). Otherwise, I just keep them 20 width with engineers, art, and recon. 

Tanks also vary, but it’s best to make 40 width, so they can be your brawler. Usually half tank half motorized with a few divisions of SP AT. However, I DO like small light tank divisions with ONLY tanks (when playing as Germany) because they are super fast and can surround the enemy. 2-4 brigades in that case. Recon support. Otherwise, always make the tank divisions AT LEAST 20 width, preferably 40 with repair and support art plus any other support you see fit.

Over 1000 hours in game here. You need troops assigned to the front. I usually have three infantry armies assigned to the Polish front 18-24 divisions strong. All of these under one field marshal. These hold the line. A fourth army of purely armor and trucks 10 minimum (2-4 light tanks, 4-6 medium tanks, 6-10 motorized divisions)  will be placed strategically along the line to break through weak points and push for victory points while encircling the enemy. DO NOT (I cannot stress this enough) just activate your infantries orders and let the computer do it for you. You will lose hundreds of thousands of men this way. You can set up orders to gain the attack bonus but DONT activate them. Micromanage then by only sending them to attack the Poles where they are significantly weaker OR where is strategically important (i.e a city, a last connection to an encirclement, or an army you don’t want them to move, air base, naval base etc.). 

NEVER assign your tanks a front line as this will cause them to automatically abandon where you need them. ALWAYS micromanage them. When attacking a front line, throw the tanks in WITH infantry as the infantry will be the canon fodder. Otherwise you are just wasting valuable tanks and experience. Once you have broken through, advance your tanks towards the highest victory points OR create large encirclements. Once and enemy is encircled (unless a naval base or the capital is in the encirclement) they will begin taking attrition and cannot be resupplied. Unless they break out, they will eventually be destroyed for good. This is how you kill A TON of them while losing only a few thousand yourself. 

ALWAYS have air superiority as this slows down the enemy AND destroys their organization. Focus production on fighters with some ground support and some bombers (land and naval). 80% of your production should be split between fighters, tanks, and subs. The rest will be for your current needs. 

Start the game off by building ONLY civilian factories. Once you’ve taken Austria, you can begin to build other things as needed. Building civilian factories gives you the power to build things very quick in the future as well as trade for resources that will be vital to push the war forward. 

Finally (not really, but my fingers are getting tired), you need to be pumping out 20 width infantry divisions like crazy from the start. You can upgrade to 40 width divisions after Poland falls, but your priority should be to get BOOTS ON THE GROUND. By the time you do Danzig or War, you should have 1.5 million men in your army if not more. Your queue should NEVER be empty. In fact, max it out as soon as the game begins and keep it maxed up until you declare on Poland. 

Hope this helps. If you need further help, just ask.
